target_concept: Explain why the length of the smallest string provides an upper bound for the longest common prefix

mcq.questionText: Why does the length of the smallest string in a set provide an upper bound for the length of the longest common prefix among those strings?
options: Because a common prefix cannot be longer than any string that contains it, the shortest string limits the maximum possible length.
Because the longest common prefix is always equal to the length of the longest string in the set.
Because processing characters beyond the shortest string would cause a runtime error due to array index out of bounds.
Because all strings share the same characters beyond the length of the shortest string, making the prefix longer.
mcq.correctAnswer: Because a common prefix cannot be longer than any string that contains it, the shortest string limits the maximum possible length.
mcq.explanation: A prefix must be a substring of every string in the collection. Therefore it cannot exceed the length of the shortest string, since that string would not contain a longer prefix. This makes the shortest string's length an upper bound for the longest common prefix.
